audit_findings.magnitude: $64.6m net purchase price plus $0.4m acquisition-date contingent-consideration fair value; $7.5m maximum contingent payment; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor excludes Eventscape, while June 2026 cash, debt and other bridge balances include the acquisition and its funding.
audit_findings.evidence: In February 2026, we acquired all of the issued and outstanding stock of Eventscape, Inc. and Eventscape U.S. Holdings Inc. (collectively, “Eventscape”) for $ 64.1 million, plus additional contingent consideration payable upon the achievement of certain future performance objectives in 2030 not to exceed $ 7.5 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. Omitting acquired earnings can understate value, while omitting post-close losses or acquisition-related interest can overstate it. The filing reports $16.9m of first-half sales and a $2.6m operating loss for Eventscape, Parallel and Geometrik together, but does not isolate Eventscape's sustainable OE. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct a consistent pre-acquisition bridge or calculate Eventscape's separately supported post-close normalized OE, associated interest and contingent claim, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require acquisition spending that OE does not capture
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth enters the 3%-6% scenarios without an explicit deduction for acquisition cash investment outside recurring OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We regularly evaluate potential mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures, strategic alliances or other investments that we believe could complement, enhance or expand our current businesses or product lines or that might otherwise offer us growth opportunities, particularly in our Architectural Specialties segment for which we have completed nine acquisitions from July 2020 through December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking dependency rather than a demonstrated current-period error. Historical acquisitions materially contributed to growth, but the filings also report organic growth and do not establish that the modeled rates require future acquisitions. Value would be overstated if acquisitions are necessary but their cost remains excluded.
audit_findings.action: Track organic OE growth separately from acquired growth; rerun any scenario shown to require acquisitions with explicit purchase-price, funding, integration and contingent-payment assumptions.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease asset consumption may be added back without its replacement cash cost
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 finance-lease amortization $6.3m and principal payments $5.8m
audit_findings.mechanism: OE may add back finance-lease asset amortization through eligible D&A while omitting principal payments or an equivalent replacement-asset charge because those payments are financing cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: We enter into operating and finance leases for certain manufacturing plants, warehouses, equipment and automobiles.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed amounts demonstrate the potential scale, but the record does not show whether the $6.3m amortization was included in eligible D&A or whether replacement cost was captured elsewhere. If both safeguards are absent, recurring OE is overstated; materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $6.3m amortization through the OE add-back and reconcile it to the $5.8m principal payment and $7.7m of finance-lease ROU additions; rerun with a normalized replacement charge if necessary.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retiree benefits are a senior claim with cash cost above reported benefit expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.2m unfunded obligation; FY2025 contributions exceeded expense by $4.7m
audit_findings.mechanism: The issue can enter through a normalized retiree-benefit cash deduction from OE or through recognition of the unfunded obligation in the equity bridge, but not both without avoiding double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: Our unfunded postretirement plan liabilities were $36.2 million as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash-versus-expense mismatch is demonstrated. The $36.2m obligation equals about $0.85 per diluted share. Alternatively, capitalizing the $4.7m annual gap using the model's most favorable bull operating-PV multiple produces about $1.82 per share. Both are small versus the $79.63 gap between the $93.70 bull value and the $173.33 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether normalized benefit payments are already deducted from OE; otherwise rerun using either a normalized annual cash charge or a bridge deduction for the obligation, with no double count.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to add equity-method stakes whose earnings remain in OE
audit_findings.mechanism: WAVE and Overcast results flow through net earnings and OE, while their $29.6m carrying value is also added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the equity method, our initial investment is recorded at cost and subsequently adjusted to recognize our share of the investee’s earnings or losses, which are included as a component of our net earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing identifies the entire $29.6m as $26.3m of WAVE and $3.3m of Overcast equity-method investments, making the double count demonstrated unless their results were purged from OE. Removing $29.6m reduces value by only about $0.69 per share, less than 1% of base equity value and immaterial to the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Remove the $29.6m stakes bridge addition and rerun per-share values, or purge affiliate earnings from OE and value the stakes separately.

audit_findings.title: Environmental claims may exceed the recorded liability
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrecorded remediation costs would reduce future OE or constitute an additional claim ahead of common equity beyond amounts already expensed and reserved.
audit_findings.evidence: We are unable to reasonably estimate our final share of the total costs associated with the interim or final remediation at the site, although such amounts may be material to any one quarter's or one year’s results of operations in the future.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 recorded reserve is $4.6m, but the company cannot estimate its final share of certain investigation and remediation costs and states that excess costs may be material to an individual period. That establishes exposure, not an additional measurable liability or a material valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain updated site estimates, PRP allocation data, insurance recoverability and payment timing; stress-test only credible costs above the recorded $4.6m reserve.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Any eligible residual D&A left as an expense understates historical OE, but the valuation uses FY2025 latest actual OE rather than the historical trend as its anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2019 $52.2m (72.4% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The computed FY2019 residual is about $19.9m because $52.2m represents 72.4% of filed D&A. Even if all of that residual qualified for addition, it would change only FY2019 OE and would not change the $235.0m FY2025 anchor or the scenario values under the stated latest-actual rule.
audit_findings.action: Classify the FY2019 residual for record completeness; rerun the valuation only if filed evidence shows the same omission affects FY2025 anchor OE.
